explanation: Earth moves about 1 degree along its orbit each day, so it must turn about 1 degree further to bring the Sun back to the same spot in the sky. That takes about 4 minutes.

claims.text: A solar day is longer than a full rotation relative to the stars because Earth also moves along its orbit around the Sun.
Earth rotates once relative to the distant stars in about 23 hours 56 minutes.
The Moon's tidal braking, the tilt of Earth's axis and leap seconds do not explain the difference of about 4 minutes between a solar day and a sidereal day.
Earth moves about 1 degree along its orbit each day.
Turning about 1 extra degree takes Earth about 4 minutes.
